value: Analyze low-level CPU microarchitecture behavior (IPC, branch prediction, cache misses, pipeline stalls) under yaml stress-ng loads

Validates that each yaml stress-ng command completes under perf stat and that IPC, branch misprediction, cache-miss, pipeline-stall, and context-switch rates are parsed, or reported as na (<reason>) when the host does not expose a PMU counter

#1: Instructions per cycle (instructions_per_cycle_ipc); #2: Branch misprediction rate, pct (branch_misprediction_rate); #3: Cache misses per 1,000 instructions (cache_misses_per_1000_instructions); #4: Pipeline stalls, pct (pipeline_stall_pct); #5: Ctx switches/s (context_switches_during_workload_switches_s)
Run apt installed Linux perf (linux-tools-$(uname -r)) as perf stat -x, -e <events> -- <stress-ng command> for each yaml workload command. stress-ng is the workload generator

perf stat -x, -o <run>/perf_N.csv -e cycles,instructions,branches,branch-misses,cache-misses,context-switches,<stall event>,<event_list> -- <workload command>. Stall event: cycle_activity.stalls_total on Intel, stalled-cycles-backend on AMD (BENCHMARK_PMU_STALL_EVENT overrides). If perf cannot open its events, the command runs without perf, the four PMU metrics read na (<reason>), and context switches come from getrusage

Run each yaml workload command under perf stat -x,, counting cycles, instructions, branches, branch-misses, cache-misses, context-switches, the stall event, and event_list. Intel uses cycle_activity.stalls_total; AMD uses stalled-cycles-backend. IPC is instructions/cycles. Mispredict percent, misses per 1,000 instructions, and stall percent are those ratios times 100, 1000, and 100. If perf cannot open events, the command still runs, the four PMU metrics read na, and context switches come from getrusage

Runs each yaml workload_commands entry under perf stat -x, and derives IPC, branch-mispredict percent, cache misses per 1,000 instructions, stall percent, and context switches/s. num_cpus substitutes into stress-ng. event_list adds perf events; unknown names are dropped. duration is seconds per command. The stall event is cycle_activity.stalls_total on Intel and stalled-cycles-backend on AMD. If perf cannot open events, the command still runs and the four PMU metrics read na. output_format: csv
CSV, one row per workload command (duplicated when only one command), plus perf_N.csv, perf_N.txt, and pmu_events.txt
one CSV row per yaml workload command

Each yaml stress-ng command exits 0, two or more samples parse into SQLite, and validation passes. The four PMU metrics are finite numbers or na (<reason>); context switches/s is always a number. Missing stress-ng or a failed workload fails the run

Each metric is the mean over workload rows. A counter perf did not count is na (<reason>), never 0 or a floor. pmu_counter_running_pct below 100 means perf multiplexed more events than hardware counters and scaled the counts. cache-misses is perf's generic event (last-level cache on Intel)
